extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO OED staff, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order from the USPTO Director resolving an OED disciplinary complaint against a registered patent practitioner; it states stipulated facts, legal conclusions identifying specific violations of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, and detailed sanctions and conditions for suspension and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — presenting checks returned for insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting checks to the USPTO on numerous occasions that were returned for insufficient funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists many specific instances (by application and check numbers/dates/amounts) where the respondent submitted checks that were returned unpaid; this conduct is treated as a violation of §10.23(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED finds that submission of returned checks and related failures constitute conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice under §10.23(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the respondent's fitness to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated returned checks and failures to fulfill client/office obligations are cited as conduct reflecting adversely on fitness under §10.23(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglecting client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting matters that clients entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order finds neglect (e.g., failing to timely respond to office actions, resulting in abandonment) to be a violation of §10.77(c). Several application abandonments are recited as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1) — failing to seek lawful objectives of clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally failing to seek the lawful objectives of clients through reasonably available means permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent's failure to take steps to preserve client applications and to timely pay fees is characterized as intentionally failing to pursue clients' lawful objectives under §10.84(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6) — intentional or habitual violation of USPTO disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally or habitually violating USPTO disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple instances of returned checks, failures to respond to OED requests, and other conduct are treated as intentional/habitual violations under §10.89(c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practicing patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for two years beginning on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is the primary sanction imposed by the Order; timing and effect are specified in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for wind-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limited recognition is expressly for winding up client matters and effectuating the required transfers and returns; the Order defines its duration and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw from employment and wind up client business (37 C.F.R. § 10.40)
rubrics_metrics.description: During limited recognition, respondent must wind up all client business before the Office and withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires withdrawal/ wind-up consistent with the cited regulatory provision; practical steps include filing necessary notices/withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While limited recognition exists for wind-up, the practitioner must not take on new matters before the USPTO during that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Notice of Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette containing specified language about the violations and suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the exact notice text to be published and directs publication pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state bars and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice to the Utah State Bar, the Ohio State Bar, appropriate employees of the Office, and interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States that the respondent has been suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative notification across jurisdictions/agencies is required as part of the sanctioning process (per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender client's active USPTO case files within 30 days (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Final Order, respondent shall surrender each client's active USPTO case file(s) to each client or another practitioner designated by each client, and file proof thereof with the OED Director within the same 30-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the specific regulatory provision and imposes a strict 30-day deadline plus proof-filing obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate in good faith with successor practitioner (no charge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate in good-faith with the practitioner to whom a file is surrendered to prevent harm to the client's interests and shall do so at no charge to the client or practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation includes assisting transfer and ensuring continuity of representation; any assistance must be provided without fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward client communications and take no further legal action (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(a) and (b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall immediately forward any communication relating to a client matter addressed to or received by him for the client or practitioner designated by the client, and shall take no other legal action in the matter, enter any appearance, or provide legal advice concerning the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves client rights during transfer; the Order references the regulatory authority for these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return unearned funds and property within 30 days (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Final Order, respondent shall return to any client having immediate or prospective business before the Office any unearned legal funds, including any unearned retainer fee, and any securities and property of the client, and shall file proof thereof with the OED Director no later than filing his petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty to return unearned funds is time-limited and requires proof to be filed with OED; the Order ties this to reinstatement documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take specified compliance steps and file affidavit of steps taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall: (1) promptly take steps to comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(b)(1)(vi), (b)(3), (b)(4), (b)(5), and (b)(6); (2) within 30 days of taking such steps, file with the OED Director an affidavit describing the precise nature of the steps taken; and (3) submit proof of compliance with §§ 11.58(b)(3), (b)(4), (b)(5), and (b)(6) upon filing a petition for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes both immediate corrective actions and documentary proof obligations that must be sworn in an affidavit and later corroborated upon reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(a), (e), and (f) as of the date of the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(a), (e), and (f) effective immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly makes compliance with these subsections an immediate requirement; those subsections govern duties on termination of representation and related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED to move to dismiss pending Complaint within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Final Order, the OED Director shall prepare and file a motion to dismiss the Complaint and Notice of Proceedings Under 35 U.S.C. § 32 pending against Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the motion to dismiss is an administrative step required by the settlement terms once the sanctions and conditions are set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and return client funds related to returned checks within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the Final Order, respondent shall determine whether he received funds from a client for each of the checks identified as being returned for insufficient funds and remaining unpaid, and if so, within 60 days return all such funds to the respective client; upon seeking reinstatement, provide OED with corroborating proof of all such payments to the clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires a factual accounting and restitution where appropriate, plus documentary proof at reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay USPTO returned check fees within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the Final Order, respondent shall pay the USPTO the amount of returned check fees identified in the stipulated facts and remaining unpaid; upon seeking reinstatement provide corroborating proof of such payments to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary payments to the Office are required on a defined schedule and must be evidenced at reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education on law office management and client trust accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Within two years of the Final Order respondent shall enroll, complete and receive CLE credit under the Rules of the Utah State Bar for at least one course where the predominant subject matter is law office management for solo practitioners or small law offices and which includes information on establishing, utilizing, and maintaining client trust accounts; upon seeking reinstatement provide corroborating proof of successful completion including documentary evidence of attendance, course content description, and copies of written materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CLE requirement is content-specific (law office management and trust accounts), time-limited (within two years), and requires detailed proof at reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the two-year suspension, respondent may apply for reinstatement by filing a petition and an affidavit showing compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 and demonstrating compliance with paragraphs 135(o), (p), and (q) of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is conditional upon both regulatory compliance and fulfillment of the specific restitution, fee-payment, and CLE obligations described in the Order; documentary corroboration is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No award of costs between the parties is made; each pays its own expenses.
